term.def: AI that can plan and carry out several steps on its own to reach a goal, instead of only answering one question at a time.

prompt.prompt: Act as a cybersecurity advisor for a [size] company in [industry]. List the five biggest risks of using AI tools at work and one simple step to reduce each.

quiz.q: You need to know coding to use AI tools well at work.
quiz.why: Most AI tools work with plain language. If you can explain a task clearly in words, you can start using them today.

quiz.q: AI tools can give confident answers that are wrong, so important facts should always be checked.
quiz.why: AI predicts likely words and does not truly know facts. It can sound sure even when it is mistaken, so checking matters.

quiz.q: If you ask an AI tool politely, it will always give a correct answer.
quiz.why: Being polite does not make an answer more accurate. Clear instructions and good context help far more than good manners.

quiz.q: Techloy has published a guide on how to choose the right AI security software for your business.
quiz.why: This is what the headline says. Choosing security tools for AI is now a topic businesses are reading about.

quiz.q: TheWire.in reports that agentic AI is coming to enterprise software.
quiz.why: That is the claim in the headline. The article also asks what this means for today's software engineers.
